text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria can tighten central bank lending as part of a currency board mechanism even before a funding deal with the International Monetary Fund is in place, Finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said.
-- Bulgaria's Central Electoral Committee (CEC) started registering political parties for the general elections in April, a CEC official said.

-- Bulgaria can introduce a currency board system in April, immediately after the parliamentary elections, Steve Hanke from the Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore said after meeting the economic advisors of the President Petar Stoyanov.

-- The European Union is prepared to discuss a balance of payments support for Bulgaria before a funding deal with the International Monetary Fund is in place, head of EU representation office in Sofia Thomas O'Sullivan said.

-- Bulgaria is expected to export to Hungary forklift trucks worth $7 million and canned food worth $2.5 million under bilateral agreements sealed during the visit of Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov in Budapest last week, Chairman of the Bulgarian Economic Chamber Bozhidar Danev said.

-- Bulgaria's Socialist Party (BSP) executive bureau discussed the Socialist cabinet's performance during its two years in office but declined to pin personal responsibility for the current economic crisis to its members, a BSP senior official said.
-- Bulgaria is expected to apply for some $100 million loan from the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank to fund social programmes, Social care minister Ivan Neikov said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim said it had lifted limits on fuel supplies to local retailers and was planning to increase processing to 16,000 tonnes of crude daily by the end of this week.
